metaDescription: Connect Salesforce to Zapier to sync leads, contacts, and opportunities automatically with your other business applications.
intro: Manual data entry between Salesforce and the rest of your stack slows down your sales pipeline. This guide shows how to connect Salesforce to Zapier, authenticate your production or sandbox environment, and map CRM fields so leads and opportunity changes trigger automated actions elsewhere.

steps.heading: Create a new Zap
steps.body: Open the Zapier dashboard and start a new workflow.

steps.heading: Select Salesforce and choose your event object
steps.body: Choose Salesforce as your trigger app and pick the object you want to track, such as a Lead or Opportunity.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Salesforce instance
steps.body: Connect either your production or sandbox environment safely.

steps.heading: Grant API access
steps.body: Approve the required OAuth API permissions and verify the account connection.

steps.heading: Fetch sample data
steps.body: Pull fresh Lead or Opportunity sample data payloads for testing your field mapping.

steps.heading: Map CRM fields and finish
steps.body: Add an action step and map dynamic Salesforce data tokens, like customer name, email, and lead source, into your target app.

faq.question: Can I connect a Salesforce sandbox instead of production?
faq.answer: Yes, you can authenticate either your Salesforce sandbox or production environment depending on what you're testing.

faq.question: What Salesforce events can trigger a Zap?
faq.answer: Triggers include events like a New Lead, an Updated Contact, or a Changed Opportunity Stage.

faq.question: What kind of data can I map from Salesforce?
faq.answer: CRM variables like customer names, email addresses, lead sources, and custom fields can all be mapped into your workflow.

faq.question: What if I hit Salesforce API limits?
faq.answer: The tutorial covers troubleshooting tips for Salesforce API limits, enterprise permissions, and connection token resets.
